review: The print gives stanza 1 as two lines and stanzas 2–5 as four; the payload follows the print. The hymn's whole shape is a chain of rhetorical questions, so every stanza after the first opens with הֲ־.

3:2–3:4 נֹשֵׂא הַיִּסּוּרִים … כַּדּוֹנַג נָמַס — Isaiah 53:4 (נֹשֵׂא מַכְאֹבֵינוּ) with Ps 22:15 (נָמֵס כַּדּוֹנַג לִבִּי); the Arabic مُحْتَمِلَ الْعَذَاب / كَالشَّمْعِ عَنِّي ذَاب is that pair, and דּוֹנַג is the psalm's wax.

4:1–4:4 הָיִיתָ לִי כָפְרִי / קָדְשִׁי וְצִדְקִי — the Arabic غَدَوْتَ لِي فِدَاي / قَدَاسَتِي بِرِّي; Hebrew turns the abstract nouns into predicates with a possessive, which is how 1 Cor 1:30 states it (נִהְיָה לָנוּ … קְדֻשָּׁה וּפְדוּת).
2:4 הֲנִדְכֵּיתָ — the Arabic سُحِقْتَ is 'were crushed', and דכא is the verb of Isa 53:5/10; the question particle sits on the line that carries the verb so the interrogative is not stranded.
5:2 הֵן רֵיקָה יָדִי — 'behold, my hand is empty'; the Arabic لَقَدْ خَلَتْ يَدِي is the same image, and the clause is cast as a verbless sentence for the beat.
